guide.summary: GitLab documents OAuth 2 for user-owned apps via authorization code flow with or without PKCE, using registered app credentials and endpoints. The read_api scope is the least-privilege documented grant for reading project issues, granting read access to all groups and projects the person can access, not per-project. The project issues list endpoint uses keyset cursor pagination, so no write permission is needed. The connected person must already hold a project role allowing issue viewing. Access tokens expire after 2 hours by default and require refresh tokens. Provider review, marketplace listing and customer-admin approval are not documented in these snapshots and remain unknown.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for Read issue titles in projects the connected person can access, including pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Register a user-owned OAuth application and use authorization code flow
findings.detail: Authorization code flows require the application to be registered first in the user's account, which yields an Application ID and Client Secret. PKCE is the recommended flow for client and server apps; standard authorization code is also documented for secure server-side apps.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer organizations connect through the OAuth application registered for this integration.

evidence.quote: registered first via the /user_settings/applications page in your user’s account.
Authorization code with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) :
Authorization code : Secure and common flow. Recommended option for secure

findings.title: read_api grants read access to the API for groups and projects
findings.detail: read_api grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects. It is read-only and does not include write scopes like api. It cannot be narrowed to a single project, so the boundary is whatever the connected person can access.
findings.appliesWhen: Only when the integration lists project issues and the connected person has project access.

evidence.quote: read_api Grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, and the package registry.
Lists all issues for a specified project.
If the project is private, you need to provide credentials to authorize.

findings.title: Connected person needs an existing project role that can view issues
findings.detail: OAuth scopes do not replace the person's project role. The Guest role can view issues only in private and internal projects. Private projects require credentials. Confirm representative account access before testing.
findings.appliesWhen: The confirmed request says the connected person can already access the project.

evidence.quote: Guest View and comment on issues and epics. Cannot push code or access repository. This role applies to private and internal projects only.
If the project is private, you need to provide credentials to authorize.

findings.title: Access tokens expire and require refresh tokens
findings.detail: By default OAuth access tokens expire after two hours (7200 seconds). Integrations must generate a new token using the refresh_token. On Self-Managed and Dedicated, administrators can configure the lifetime.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to every connected organization's token lifecycle.

evidence.quote: By default, access tokens expire after two hours (7200 seconds). Integrations that use access tokens must generate a new token with the refresh_token attribute. Refresh tokens can be used even
On GitLab Self-Managed and GitLab Dedicated, administrators can configure the token lifetime. For more information, see modify OAuth access token maximum lifetime .

findings.title: Send the OAuth token as a Bearer header on API requests
findings.detail: After token exchange, the access token is sent with the Authorization Bearer header to the API. The token can be passed as a GET parameter or in the header, but not both.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to the issue-list API calls.

evidence.quote: The access token allows you to make requests to the API on behalf of a user.
--header "Authorization: Bearer <OAUTH-TOKEN>" \
You can pass the token either as a GET parameter or in the Authorization header, but not both.

steps.doneWhen: The application shows an Application ID and Client Secret, and the redirect URI matches the one used in the token exchange.

steps.title: Obtain consent via authorization code flow with read_api scope
steps.detail: Redirect the connected person to the authorization endpoint with scope=read_api, then receive the returned code at the redirect URI. This consent step is performed by the connected person; the agent does not execute it.

steps.title: Request the next page of project issues using the keyset cursor
steps.detail: Repeat the project issues request for the same project, adding the cursor query parameter with the keyset cursor value from the prior page, using the same Bearer token. Do not combine this with offset page or per_page navigation. Representative input: a project the connected person can already view. Expected result: a JSON array of issue objects each containing a title field. steps.doneWhen: Done only when a documented end condition is observed; an empty page alone is not a supported stop rule. Boundary check: confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to the project issues endpoint and no create, update or delete requests.
